H2S Hazard Awareness & Properties

HYDROGEN SULFIDE (H2S) PROPERTIES:

• Color: Colorless gas • Odor: Rotten eggs (at low concentrations)

• Odor threshold: 0.0005 - 0.1 ppm • Olfactory fatigue: Occurs rapidly (>100 ppm)

• Specific Gravity: 1.19 (heavier than air) • Flammable range: 4.3% - 46% in air

• IDLH (Immediately Dangerous to Life and Health): 100 ppm

• PEL (Permissible Exposure Limit - OSHA): 10 ppm (8-hour TWA)

• STEL (Short Term Exposure Limit - 15 min): 15 ppm

H2S EXPOSURE EFFECTS:

CONCENTRATIONEFFECTS
0.01 - 1.5 ppm 2 - 5 ppm 10 - 20 ppm 20 - 100 ppm 100 - 200 ppm 200 - 300 ppm 300 - 500 ppm 500 - 1000 ppm >1000 ppmOdor threshold (rotten eggs) Moderate odor, possible headache, nausea Eye irritation, permissible exposure limit Fatigue, loss of appetite, headache, irritability, poor memory, dizziness Severe eye and respiratory irritation, olfactory fatigue (cannot smell) Severe inflammation of eyes/throat, pulmonary edema, loss of consciousness Pulmonary edema, unconsciousness, respiratory paralysis, death Rapid unconsciousness, respiratory arrest, death within minutes Immediate respiratory paralysis, coma, death within seconds

EMERGENCY PROCEDURES:

IF H2S ALARM ACTIVATES:

1. ALL PERSONNEL - EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY to upwind assembly area

2. Attendant - Account for all entrants, do not enter to rescue

3. Entry Supervisor - Initiate emergency response, contact rescue team

4. Rescue Team - Don SCBA, perform rescue if safe to do so

5. Do NOT enter without SCBA - H2S is immediately fatal

IF PERSONNEL COLLAPSE / UNCONSCIOUS:

1. DO NOT ENTER WITHOUT SCBA - Rescuers become victims

2. Rescue Team with SCBA to retrieve victim

3. Move victim to fresh air immediately

4. Administer CPR if trained and equipped

5. Administer oxygen if available and trained

6. Seek immediate medical attention
